learning_need: Current broad scientific and ethical good-practice framework for clinical-trial design, conduct and oversight
decision_rationale: WHO's 2026 course is the strongest broad current clinical-trials recommendation in the pool. Nine interactive modules translate the 2024 WHO guidance into five scientific and ethical principles using real-world cases and decision-making. It is broader than compliance-only GCP and newer than the other specialist routes.
marginal_value: Adds a current principles-and-practice framework spanning design, conduct and oversight rather than one narrow compliance function.
provider_concentration_notes: WHO is not otherwise concentrated in the canonical Health set.
coverage_notes: Complements rather than replaces TGHN GCP, ethics and data-governance specialists.

learning_need: Current ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice compliance training
decision_rationale: TGHN GCP E6(R3) earns a separate slot because it serves a sharply defined professional need: current ICH GCP compliance. Its eight modules are aligned to the final E6(R3), available in multiple languages and end in a free assessed certificate. WHO remains broader on trial principles and implementation.
marginal_value: Adds explicit GCP compliance training, multilingual access and verified credential mechanics.
provider_concentration_notes: TGHN has several strong survivors; this one is retained because GCP is a distinct professional requirement.
coverage_notes: Complements WHO clinical-trial principles rather than duplicating them.

learning_need: Applied research ethics for health and clinical research
decision_rationale: Research Ethics V2 covers a distinct role through ten modules on risks/benefits, vulnerability, participant obligations, community engagement, privacy, consent and ethical dilemmas. Its case-oriented practice and module certification materially improve the clinical-research pathway beyond GCP compliance.
marginal_value: Adds substantive ethics depth that neither GCP nor the broader WHO course develops as fully.
provider_concentration_notes: A second TGHN admission is justified by a separate professional competency rather than provider breadth.
coverage_notes: Forms the ethics layer in a broader research-practice pathway.

learning_need: Responsible health-research data governance, sharing and lifecycle practice
decision_rationale: The Data Life Cycle fills a data-governance role not covered by GCP or research ethics: management, sharing principles, governance/access, quality, costs and repositories. It is current, peer-reviewed and directly relevant to reproducible health research.
marginal_value: Adds a distinct health-research data stewardship competency.
provider_concentration_notes: The third TGHN admission is justified because data governance is a separate learning need from GCP and ethics.
coverage_notes: Not a full data-manager or statistics qualification; admitted as a research-data-governance foundation.

learning_need: Nutrition-sensitive agriculture and food-systems policy/programme practice
decision_rationale: This course fills a distinct public-health/nutrition systems role absent from the clinical-research cluster. Its scenario-based five-lesson route connects malnutrition, agriculture and food systems with nutrition-sensitive policy, investments and programmes and includes a free assessed badge.
marginal_value: Adds professional nutrition/food-systems coverage not served elsewhere in the canonical Health set.
provider_concentration_notes: Only the stronger FAO nutrition course is retained; the basic concepts micro-module is rejected.
coverage_notes: Currentness is weaker than the clinical-research leaders, so the course receives a shorter review cadence than stable academic subjects.

learning_need: Very short introductory nutrition, food-security and livelihoods concepts
decision_rationale: At roughly 30–35 minutes, this is a useful orientation but far below the depth and practice bar for a canonical course. The stronger FAO nutrition-through-food-systems route already covers the professional learning need with scenarios and assessment.
marginal_value: Adds basic terminology but no distinct core learning pathway.
provider_concentration_notes: FAO concentration is controlled by retaining only the stronger professional course.
coverage_notes: Basic concepts remain accessible as a supplementary module.

learning_need: Introductory Good Clinical Laboratory Practice orientation
decision_rationale: GCLP is useful but only 60–120 minutes, with limited practice and weaker currency evidence. It is too small to justify a fourth TGHN core slot when GCP, ethics and data governance already form a stronger research-practice pathway.
marginal_value: Adds laboratory-specific orientation but insufficient depth for canonical promotion.
provider_concentration_notes: Provider concentration reinforces the decision after three clearly stronger TGHN roles are retained.
coverage_notes: Remains a useful specialist supplement for laboratory staff.

learning_need: Introductory chemical-hazard readiness for health and emergency professionals
decision_rationale: Part I is current and authoritative, but its intrinsic depth is limited and the intended Part II remains on shallow hold because granular public evidence is insufficient. Promoting Part I alone would create an incomplete chemical-hazards pathway and overstate the verified educational package.
marginal_value: Adds specialist hazard awareness but not enough standalone depth while the series remains incomplete.
provider_concentration_notes: Provider authority is not an admission substitute.
coverage_notes: Chemical-hazard training remains an explicit unresolved coverage area until Part II evidence or a stronger complete alternative is verified.
